subject: Benchmarking & acceptance cadence for AuroraHealth onboarding
messages:
From: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@aurorahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@aurorahealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Benchmarking & acceptance criteria for Redwood onboarding

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our infra and SRE teams want to lock down the acceptance criteria and a simple schedule for the performance run so we can sign off on the Dedicated deployment. High level asks from our side:
- Latency: p95 for 512-token generation should be <= 280ms; p99 <= 520ms (90% of requests).
- Throughput: sustain 80 concurrent sessions with average 20 tokens/sec per session for 30 minutes without tail loss.
- Error budget: total 5xxs <= 0.1% during the run.

We can provide test harness access and a staging dataset. Can you send a playbook that spells out responsibilities, what logs/artifacts you need, and the schedule (preferred window: next week)?

Also, we require SOC2 evidence and a short runbook snapshot for our security review (we can accept a stubbed file).

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Wu
Director, Platform Engineering
AuroraHealth
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: ops@aurorahealth.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Benchmarking & acceptance criteria for Redwood onboarding

Hi Daniel —

Appreciate the clarity — we've captured the targets below and sketched a minimal acceptance runbook. Attaching a proposed benchmark plan (aurora_benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx) with the steps and artifacts we will share. Summary here: 

Acceptance targets (as you requested):
- Latency targets: p95 <= 280ms, p99 <= 520ms (measured at gateway, 512-token prompt).
- Throughput targets: sustain 80 concurrent sessions, 20 tokens/s avg/session for 30min sustained window.
- Error budget: 5xx <= 0.1% across run.

Planned schedule:
- Pre-run sync (30m): Thu 2025-06-19 14:00 UTC — confirm test users, traffic shape, and dataset.
- Dry run (30m): Mon 2025-06-23 02:00 UTC — internal only to validate tooling.
- Acceptance run (30m sustained window within 60m ramp): Tue 2025-06-24 03:00 UTC (we'll hold a 90m window for retries).

Responsibilities:
- Redwood (CS/Infra): run generation jobs, collect telemetry (latency percentiles, GPU util, KV cache hit rates), produce artifacts: loadtest_results_20250624.csv, aggregate latency plots, and an evidence bundle.
- Aurora SRE: provide test harness endpoints, firewall exceptions, and a list of representative prompts; validate SOC2 stub and runbook snapshot.

Artifacts we'll provide after the run: raw request logs (redacted), aggregated percentiles, CPU/GPU telemetry, and a runbook snapshot for security review.

Quick note on measurement: we'll compute p95/p99 at the gateway ingress (client-observed latencies) and reconcile with model-serving traces. If any discrepancy > 10%, we'll include a reconciliation section.

Attachments: aurora_benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — outline, payload samples, and measurement scripts.

If that works, I'll loop in Monica and Tessa to own load generation and evidence collection.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 09:08:00 -0400
Subject: FW: Benchmarking & acceptance cadence for AuroraHealth onboarding

Monica / Tessa —

Looping you both in to take operational ownership for Aurora's acceptance run next week. Action items: 
- Monica: set up the load harness (we'll use k6 + our traffic-shaper); confirm the 80 concurrent sessions profile and implement the 60m ramp (10m warmup, 30m sustained, 20m cool-down). Please place the harness in our staging cluster and share the run command.
- Tessa: own telemetry collection and artifacts. Please ensure we capture: request-level latencies, status codes, GPU util, KV cache hit/miss rates, and Gateway-level ingress metrics. Prepare the results CSV template (columns: timestamp, request_id, latency_ms, status_code, model_variant, gpu_util_pct).

I'll run the dry and acceptance runs from the control plane and coordinate comms with Aurora. Keep notes in the runbook_snapshot.txt and upload final artifacts to the Drive folder (link below) after the run.

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AuroraBenchmark
HubSpot: HS-89321

Thanks — let me know if any blocker.

-K
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Wu <daniel.wu@aurorahealth.com>, ops@aurorahealth.com
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jun 2025 14:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Benchmarking & acceptance cadence for AuroraHealth onboarding

Hi Daniel —

We completed the acceptance run today (summary and artifacts attached). Key results: 
- Latency: p95 = 262ms, p99 = 498ms (measured at gateway, 512-token window) — both within targets.
- Throughput: sustained 82 concurrent sessions, avg 21.4 tokens/sec/session across the 30m sustained window.
- Error budget: observed 0.04% 5xx (below 0.1% threshold).

We've attached: loadtest_results_20250624.csv (raw row-level data), runbook_snapshot.txt (what we ran, configs), and a filled aurora_benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx with notes. Artifacts uploaded to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AuroraBenchmark

Notes / observations: 
- KV cache hit-rate dropped by ~6% during the cool down; we recommend a short cache-warmup script if Aurora intends to run frequent bursts.
- GPU util peaked at 78% on the largest instance pool — capacity margin is healthy, but if you plan to increase concurrency by >20% we should provision an additional node beforehand.

Next steps / asks from Aurora: 
1) Please confirm acceptance sign-off on these metrics or flag any concerns by EOD Fri 2025-06-27.
2) If accepted, we'll schedule a short handoff with the Dedicated provisioning team to finalize capacity and SLA attachments.
3) We'll prepare a one-page evidence packet for your security team (SOC2 artifacts + runbook snapshot) — let us know any extra items to include.

Attachments: loadtest_results_20250624.csv (spreadsheet), runbook_snapshot.txt (text), aurora_benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks and congrats to the team — nice run.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
